lessons: Remote interactive bash had history expansion enabled, which silently mangled heredocs containing '!'. Fix: prefix remote commands with 'set +H', or better, transfer file content via stdin piping ('threadripper-ssh cat > dest < localfile') so content never passes through shell parsing.

A test file outside hardhat's test/ dir can resolve a different chai copy than the one hardhat-chai-matchers patches, making matcher assertions (revertedWith) throw 'Invalid Chai property'. Keep matcher-based regression tests under packages/contracts/test/; use try/catch style for devteam/repro/ artifacts.

next_action.reason: W3B-001 is implemented and verified (222/222 Hardhat green, replay blocked, fresh claims work). Queue head is now BLD-001 (next@16.2.6 critical, effort XS). Note: MUS-001 needs a Dino decision and stays parked; DOC-001 (legal page false claims) is also S1/QUEUED.

root_cause: The attestor-signed claim message was keccak256(seeder, arweaveTxId, claimedAmount, chainId) with no nonce, timestamp, or expiry; the only replay throttle was the 1-day per-seeder cooldown, and MAX_REPORT_AGE was declared but never referenced in submitSeedingReport. One legitimate signature could therefore be resubmitted every cooldown window indefinitely.

summary: W3B-001 fixed: SeederCredits.submitSeedingReport no longer accepts replayed attestor signatures. The signed message now includes reportTimestamp + attestor-chosen nonce; the contract enforces MAX_REPORT_AGE (declared but previously unenforced), rejects future-dated reports, and keeps a consume-once registry (consumedReports) keyed by message hash, set AFTER signature verification so an invalid signature cannot burn a valid report. Before: one 1000-credit signature replayed after the cooldown minted 2000 credits (reproduced). After: identical replay reverts 'Report already claimed'; stale (>7d) and future-dated reports revert; a fresh signed report (new nonce) still credits normally. Absorbs SEC-012 and MUS-006 (same root cause). Contracts remain UNAUDITED — no audit claim added anywhere.
